Electives.Course Description: Science communication; concepts and practical aspects of social media; scientific reading; concepts of journalistic text production.
Course Content: Introduction to Science Communication and its Social Relevance: the role of science in society and the importance of scientific communication; science communication as a tool for inclusion and access to knowledge; the impact of social media and digital media on the dissemination of science

Communication Strategies and Dialogicity in Science Communication: techniques for making scientific content accessible to different audiences; interaction with the community to identify relevant topics; language and content adaptation for different media (video, text, audio)

Co-creation and Production of Scientific Content for the Community: science communication workshops in schools and community spaces; production of teaching materials on technology and computing for diverse audiences; planning and execution of educational campaigns on topics such as digital privacy, artificial intelligence, and the social impact of computing

Use of Digital Technologies for Science Communication: tools for producing videos, podcasts, and infographics; strategies for boosting content on social media; monitoring and analysis of the impact of outreach initiatives

Impact Assessment and Critical Reflection on Science Communication: collection of feedback from the community served; reflection on transforming academic knowledge into accessible information; records of good practices and systematization of lessons learned

\textbf{Community Profile:} The course BCC132 - Science Communication aims to bring the university closer to society through accessible communication of scientific and technological knowledge. Its target audience includes schools, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), cultural collectives, entrepreneurs, teachers, and communities with limited access to scientific information. Students will act as knowledge mediators, turning computer science concepts into content that is understandable and applicable to the daily life of the population. Interaction with the community will be participatory and dialogic, ensuring that the topics addressed in the course are defined based on the interests and needs of society. In this way, the course contributes to the democratization of knowledge and to the strengthening of digital and scientific inclusion.

\textbf{Extension Objectives:} The course aims to (i) promote the democratization of scientific and technological knowledge, making computing accessible to diverse audiences through science communication strategies, (ii) foster dialogic interaction between the university and the community, allowing the topics addressed in the course to be built collectively based on social demands, (iii) train students to communicate scientific concepts in an accessible way, developing writing and speaking skills and the use of technologies to popularize science, (iv) encourage the production of educational content by promoting workshops, digital materials, and informational campaigns on relevant computing topics, and (v) assess the impact of science communication on the community, ensuring that the actions carried out have a concrete effect on the dissemination of knowledge and on social engagement.

Electives.Course Description: Software Development Processes. Software Requirements Engineering. Software Project Management. Software as a Service (SaaS). DevOps.
Course Content: Development Processes: importance of processes for team productivity and product quality assurance; types of processes (sequential or cyclical, incremental and/or evolutionary); plan-driven processes (waterfall, spiral, Rational Unified Process); agile processes (Agile Manifesto, main characteristics, main differences between XP, Scrum and Kanban, criticisms of agile methods); Extreme Programming (historical context, principles and values, customer representative and user stories, iterations and releases, effort estimation, programming practices, project management); Scrum (historical context, development cycles, roles, artifacts, ceremonies); Kanban (historical context, product backlog, Kanban board, WIP limits)

Requirements Engineering: types of requirements (functional, non-functional, interface); object-oriented requirements elicitation and analysis techniques; requirements specification (behavior-driven development - BDD, user stories and test scenarios, use cases, UML use case diagrams); minimum viable product (MVP); A/B testing

Project Management: methods and techniques for project management based on the 10 PMI - Project Management Institute knowledge areas (scope, time, cost, quality, human resources, communications, risk, procurement, stakeholders and integration); techniques for defining the product backlog and work breakdown structure (WBS); team mobilization (processes, organization, roles and responsibilities, traceability, problem solving); effort estimation and pricing; tools for monitoring and controlling software development processes (Jira and Git)

Software as a Service (SaaS): introduction and historical context; basic concepts (Service-Oriented Architecture - SOA, Software as a Service, Cloud Computing); SaaS application architecture (client-server versus peer-to-peer architecture, web clients and scripting languages, communication via HTTP and URIs, representation via HTML and CSS, 3-tier architecture and horizontal scalability, Model-View-Controller - MVC architecture); SaaS application performance (responsiveness and availability, monitoring and bottleneck identification, use of caching, database queries); security: protection of customer data and the Brazilian General Data Protection Law (LGPD)

DevOps: version control (concepts, tools, multi-repositories versus mono-repositories); Continuous Integration - CI (motivation, concepts such as master/trunk, branches, merges, integration conflicts, gitflow); Continuous Delivery - CD (deployment, delivery, feature flags, release flags and business flags); tools for source code version control and CI/CD pipeline automation (Git)
